I worked each expected output by hand from the structure of the problem. Any valid final grid corresponds to a row permutation p and a column permutation q with B[i][j] = A[p(i)][q(j)]. The cost is inv(p) + inv(q), the number of adjacent swaps each needs, and the minimum is taken over all valid (p, q). Two of the cases (the duplicate-value 2x2 and the duplicate-value 2x3) involve several valid choices, so their answers come from comparing those choices.
